sources.citation: Snider, Keith L. 1989. The vowels of proto-Guang. Journal of West African Languages 19(2): 29-50.
sources.quote: Although the Guang languages are tonal, since tone has played no role in the historical development of the vowel system, I ignore all tonal distinctions in the data in order to keep the examples as uncomplicated as possible.
sources.locator: p. 31, footnote (it follows fn. 2 on p. 30); sample statement p. 30 para. 1
sources.note: States (p. 31, footnote to the Appendix A data note) that the Guang languages of the study - Gichode among them - are tonal, and that all tonal distinctions are deliberately left out of the cited data because tone played no role in the history of the vowel system. No inventory of tones, no tone rules, no Gikyode-specific tone facts; the tone description for these data is in the author's 'Tone in proto-Guang nouns' (ALC 3(1), 1990, an earlier listing, paywalled) and the tone-marked wordlist itself (a work listed here #6).
